heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Sainsmart Glow TPU exceptionally well out of the box thanks to its standard hardened steel nozzle and direct-drive extruder. By capping maximum volumetric speed at 4 mm³/s, the system achieves consistent extrusion up to a safe maximum print speed of 48 mm/s without risking toolhead clogs or jams.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Glue Stick (acting as a release agent to prevent PEI damage)
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 4.0 mm³/s in the filament profile to avoid exceeding the melt rate and jamming the direct drive extruder.
Bypass the Bambu AMS entirely and feed directly from an external dry box or the rear spool holder through the PTFE tube to prevent flexible filament binding.
Set Retraction Distance to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s and enable 'Wipe while Retracting' to minimize oozing and stringing common to phosphorescent TPU.
Keep the chamber door cracked open or remove the top glass lid during printing to prevent heat creep inside the enclosed X1C chamber.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder gear grinding and filament buckling before nozzle entry
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Volumetric speed set too high or heat creep softening the flexible filament in the extruder gears.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce Maximum Volumetric Speed to 3.5-4.0 mm³/s, prop open the top glass lid, and loosen the extruder idler tension if accessible.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and heavy cobwebbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the hygroscopic TPU combined with excessive nozzle temperature or disabled retraction.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament at 55°C for 6-8 hours, lower nozzle temperature to 220°C, and enable Avoid Crossing Wall surfaces in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Print permanently fusing to the build plate and tearing the coating
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: TPU creates an excessively strong molecular bond directly to clean PEI surfaces when heated.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick or liquid release agent across the Textured PEI Plate prior to starting the print.

faq.question: Can I run Sainsmart Glow TPU through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: No, flexible TPU filaments (especially abrasive glow-in-the-dark variants) will compress, buckle, and jam inside the AMS feeder funnels and internal multiplexer pathways; always feed it from the external spool holder.

faq.question: Will phosphorescent Glow TPU wear down my stock X1C nozzle?
faq.answer: No, the Bambu Lab X1C comes standard with a hardened steel nozzle and hardened extruder gears, which are fully rated to withstand abrasive additives like strontium aluminate found in glow TPU.

faq.question: Why does my print look milky and fail to glow brightly?
faq.answer: Under-extrusion or thin wall thickness limits glow pigment density; increase wall loops to at least 3 or 4 and ensure filament is thoroughly dried to maintain full light-trapping density.

faq.question: Should the X1C enclosure door stay closed while printing TPU?
faq.answer: No, leave the front door slightly ajar or vent the top glass panel to keep internal chamber temperatures cool and eliminate the risk of heat creep softening the filament.
